page: Microsoft Azure B32ls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bsv2 series. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It provides 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU supports vector and cryptography instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, paired with 48 MB of L3 cache.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This low memory-to-vCPU ratio aligns with compute-leaning burstable architectures. The instance contains no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote Azure storage options for persistence and operating system disks. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present. Benchmarked uncached memory bandwidth reaches 142.03 GB/sec for large-block reads and 66.03 GB/sec for writes.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute suites, scoring 1634.0 in Geekbench single-core and 13883.0 in multi-core evaluations. Stress-ng scores show 1899.38 in single-core and 31040.35 in multi-core metrics. In real-world simulation tasks, it handles static web serving at 33.06 GB/sec and manages 32.15 million Redis SET operations per second. While small-scale LLM generation (135M model) performs strongly at 292.79 tokens per second, large models such as 70B demonstrate weak throughput at 6.5 tokens per second during prompt ingestion.

Given its burstable CPU credit allocation and low memory footprint, the instance offers cost-efficient scaling for intermittent processing rather than continuous sustained load. Best-fit deployments include batch compilation pipelines, bursty application servers, CI/CD runners, and variable-traffic web services that do not require dense RAM footprints or onboard NVMe storage.
